newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European markets ride out U.S. rate fears.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European markets ride out U.S. rate fears.

text.p: European stocks and bonds rallied strongly on Tuesday as investors refused to be spooked by the prospect of the first U.S. interest rate rise in more than two years.
All three of Europe's major bourses -- London, Paris and Frankfurt -- made good gains, with London breaking a six-day losing streak.
By the time European markets closed, Wall Street was up around 20 points, building on Monday's 100.46 point gain in volatile trading.
On the foreign exchange market the dollar gained ground above 1.69 marks and eyed 124 yen as dealers awaited the outcome of a policy-making meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve.
"The problem for the dollar is that you never know whether it will take its lead from rates or asset markets," said David Bloom, currency strategist at HSBC Markets in London.
German government bonds also firmed with British bonds or gilts, taking their cue from a rally in U.S. bonds. The U.S. long bond was up about 8/32 to yield 6.90 percent as European markets closed.
Investor focus stayed firmly on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), which was due to announce the result of its deliberations after 1900 GMT, long after the close of European markets.

"We think a 25 basis point rate hike is more likely than not," said Trevor Greetham, global strategist at Merrill Lynch. "There is certainly enough economic evidence for Greenspan to be raising rates today and on every previous ocassion of Fed tightening stock markets have come down, so equity market sentiment is likely to deteriorate."
Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan laid the ground for a possible rise last week when he stressed to a Congressional committee the importance to the economy of keeping inflation under control.

Should the FOMC exceed expectations by deciding to raise rates by half a percentage point, share markets are likely to fall on both sides of the Atlantic. No rate increase could spark an initial, but short-lived rally, analysts said.
London blue chips, which fell 4.7 percent during the six sessions up until Monday, rebounded more than one percent over the day.
The benchmark FTSE 100 index finished 55.9 points higher at 4,270.7, just below the day's best levels. The previous six sessions had taken 209 points off the index.
Among individual stocks, Shares in Lloyds TSB Plc led banks out of their recent slump, rising 29p to 483p, as HSBC James Capel repeated its "overweight" stance on the sector.

Germany's banking sector helped the blue chip DAX-30 index close floor trade just short of its high of the day with a 27.3 point gain to 3,349.14. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index climbed more than two percent.
Deutsche Bank was up 3.31 percent at 91.38 marks in late IBIS DAX trade, with dealers putting the rise down to continued speculation about mergers in the sector.

However, dealers said they were surprised at the banking sector's resilience following its role in this week's failed takeover attempt of the giant engineering company Thyssen AG by the smaller Krupp-Hoesch.
"The performance of the banks is all the more remarkable today given the disgraceful failure of Germany's first hostile takeover," a trader said.
Wall Street's strong start also underpinned the French equity market which closed with the blue-chip CAC-40 index showing a 1.74 percent rise to 2,624.25.
After flirting with a return below the key 2,600 level, French shares rose with the rest of Europe, although the strength of the rally surprised some traders.

Utility Lyonnaise des Eaux and Cie de Suez remained active on merger speculation. Lyonnaise closed 0.35 percent down at 572 francs and Suez gained 1.33 percent to 281 francs after an article in Le Monde suggested the merger would take the form of a Lyonnaise bid for Suez, instead of the other way around.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6923 marks and 123.85 yen compared with 1.6874 and 122.85 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS -- CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 55.9 points, or 1.33 percent, at 4,270.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 44.97 points, or 1.74 percent, at 2,624.25.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed floor trade up 27.3 points, or 0.82 percent, at 3,349.14. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended up 2.19 percent at 3,374.93
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $349.15 versus $350.75 on Monday. Silver finished one cent lower at $5.13.
